answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each identity costly to mint and cheap to verify: an agent must lock a refundable stake and pass a rate-limited, uniqueness-checked proof before joining, so spinning up thousands of sock puppets costs real resources while an honest agent pays once. Like an opal that gains value only after cutting, identity gains weight through staked history; a zephyr of fake accounts disperses against that cost barrier, and no lone attacker can flood the ocean of honest attestations without bankrupting itself.
